name: Portugal
summary: EU citizens only register after 3 months. Non-EU citizens (US and others) can use the D7 (passive income of about EUR 11,040 a year), the D8 (remote income of EUR 44,160 a year), or the Golden Visa from EUR 250,000 (donation) or EUR 500,000 (fund). Property no longer qualifies.
naturalisation: Lei Organica 1/2026 (in force 19 May 2026): 10 years of legal residence for most nationalities, 7 years for EU and Portuguese-speaking-country citizens; Portuguese language (A2 level reported) and civic knowledge. Applications filed on or before 18 May 2026 stay under the old 5-year rule. Counted from permit issue, per one law firm.
dual_citizenship_note: Portugal does not require renouncing another nationality (from general knowledge; not re-sourced).

routes.family: Spouse or partner and dependants have derived rights.
routes.tax_note: Registration does not itself decide tax residence; Portugal's 183-day / habitual-home test applies.
routes.name: EU free movement (registration certificate)
routes.summary: EU citizens may live in Portugal without a visa and register with the municipality after 3 months.
routes.requirements: Valid ID or passport. Beyond 3 months, workers, self-employed people, students and the economically inactive (sufficient resources and health cover) register. Permanent right of residence after 5 years of continuous legal residence (EU law, Directive 2004/38).
routes.physical_presence: No minimum beyond living in Portugal; absence over 6 months a year can break continuity

routes.processing_time: Sources quote 18 to 36 months to the first card; not confirmed by AIMA.
routes.family: Spouse or partner, dependent children and dependent parents can be included.
routes.tax_note: A permit does not make you tax resident. NHR closed to new entrants after 2023; the IFICI regime covers certain professions.
routes.name: Golden Visa (ARI): regulated investment fund
routes.summary: A residence permit for investing at least EUR 500,000 in a regulated fund that invests mainly in Portuguese companies. Real estate no longer qualifies.
routes.requirements: CMVM-regulated fund, maturity of at least 5 years, at least 60% invested in Portuguese companies, no real estate exposure. Investment must be kept for at least 5 years. Real estate, property funds and the EUR 1.5 million capital-transfer option were removed in October 2023. Lei 23/2007 art. 90-A (statute text not retrieved directly; amounts from Connaught Law, a law firm). Not open to EU/EEA/Swiss citizens (they use free movement). Permit 2 years, renewable in 2-year periods.
routes.physical_presence: Average 7 days in the first year and 14 days in each later 2-year period

Real estate, property funds and the EUR 1.5 million capital-transfer option were removed in October 2023. routes.summary: Property purchase (EUR 500,000 and up), property funds and a EUR 1.5 million capital transfer no longer give a permit.

routes.family: Spouse, children and dependent parents can join; each adds to the income and savings test.
routes.tax_note: A permit does not make you tax resident; 183 days or a habitual home in Portugal does.
routes.name: D7 residence visa (passive income / retirees)
routes.summary: For people living on pensions, rent or dividends: show regular passive income of at least the minimum wage (EUR 920 a month in 2026) and a home in Portugal.
routes.requirements: Passive income of about EUR 920 a month (2026 minimum wage), i.e. EUR 11,040 a year; spouse adds 50%, each child 30%. Savings about 12 months of income (EUR 11,040) in a Portuguese account. Accommodation, typically a 12-month lease. Pensions, rent, dividends count; salary or freelance does not. The threshold is a consular practice tied to the minimum wage, not a fixed statutory figure.
routes.physical_presence: Up to 6 consecutive months and 8 months in total abroad per permit period

routes.tax_note: Working from Portugal can create tax residence after 183 days.
routes.name: D8 digital nomad visa
routes.summary: For remote workers earning four times the Portuguese minimum wage (EUR 3,680 a month in 2026) from clients or an employer outside Portugal.
routes.requirements: Income of at least EUR 3,680 a month (4x EUR 920), from outside Portugal; savings of about EUR 11,040; accommodation; clean record. Temporary-stay visa (12 months) or residence visa (4 months, then a 2-year permit).
routes.physical_presence: Residence permit: no fixed day count stated in sources; absences should stay short (open question)

routes.name: D2 entrepreneur / independent professional visa
routes.summary: For people starting a business or working independently in Portugal; needs a business plan and proof of means.
routes.requirements: Business plan or service contracts and means of subsistence. Thresholds not sourced here (Lei 23/2007 arts. 88 and 89).

routes.name: Work permits (D1 employee, D3 highly qualified, job-seeker)
routes.summary: Non-EU workers need a job offer or contract and a work visa; highly qualified workers have a fast track.
routes.requirements: Employment contract or promise of one and a work visa from a consulate, then an AIMA residence permit. Details not researched in depth.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Portugal; no fixed day count sourced

open_questions: Official AIMA/Diario da Republica text of Lei 23/2007 art. 90-A and Lei Organica 1/2026 not retrieved directly; figures come from law-firm and press pages.
Government fees (visa, AIMA permit, ARI application) not sourced.
D7 threshold is consular practice (EUR 920 a month in 2026); official consulate figure not confirmed.
Minimum physical presence for D8 and D2/D3 not sourced.
Whether the 10-year naturalisation clock counts from first permit or application: sources differ.
